parts.method:
Part 0 found no misattributions, because the bug cannot fire in 2012-2015 notices.

Draw: /v1/notices ignores date bounds, so the draw went through tenders. For each of the 48 months from 2012-01 to 2015-12, I picked one seeded random OJ S day (Tue-Sat) and listed /v1/tenders?source=ted&published_after=D&published_before=D+1&limit=1000 (up to 2 pages). I dropped rows whose submission_deadline is on or after published_at, because their current version is a contract notice. The remaining rows were shuffled with a seed. Each was probed with /v1/notices?source=ted&publication_id=<pub>, then /v1/notices/{id}/content (the parse layer, which is exactly what read_legacy_results reads). Probing stopped at 2 multi-lot CANs per month, or 3 in one seeded month per year, giving 25 per year and 100 in total. A day was replaced after 60 probes or if it had fewer than 100 rows; none needed replacing. That came to 48 days and 595 probes: 100 multi-lot CANs, 342 single-award CANs, 26 multi-award CANs with no LOT_NO, 2 with one LOT_NO and 125 non-CANs (PIN, CN, VEAT and others).

A multi-lot CAN here means: profile ted-export-r208 or r209, TED-TD_DOCUMENT_TYPE 7, at least 2 LotResult sections, and at least 2 distinct award LOT_NO/LOT_NUMBER values.

Mapping: I re-implemented project.rs read_legacy_results as written. lot_by_no takes the TED-LOT_NO, TED-LOT_NUMBER and TED-ITEM Id values of Lot/LotsGroup/Part sections, and the first section to claim a string wins. Each award block (LotResult, values found through enclosing) then sets lot_key = lot_by_no.get(v) for every one of its three key fields in turn. The last one decides and resets lot_key to None on a miss. In the r209 walker, TED-ITEM is emitted when the section opens, so LOT_NO comes after it. I ran the mapping in two value orders:
- the notice_ids PRIMARY KEY order (section_id, field_id, ordinal), which parsed_chunk and parsed_by_ids return;
- the walker's document order.
They differ only when a notice has 10 or more lot sections.

The correct mapping is: award LOT_NO goes to the lot section publishing the same LOT_NO, with a normalised match as fallback. A notice counts as at risk when a lot section's ITEM differs from its LOT_NO and that ITEM equals another section's LOT_NO or an award's LOT_NO.

Result: all 595 probes were ted-export-r208, with no r2.0.9 at all before 2016. All 470 CANs among them, including the 100 multi-lot ones, carry zero Lot-kind sections. R2.0.8 award forms repeat AWARD_OF_CONTRACT with LOT_NUMBER and have no OBJECT_DESCR. So lot_by_no is always empty and all 906 award blocks resolve to lot_key = None, which means at-risk is 0 and misattributed is 0. Only one award block had an ITEM different from its LOT_NUMBER, and that is harmless.

API check: I read /v1/tenders/{id} for 8 hits whose tenders have 2 or more lots (2 per year): 4748635, 4730243, 4945774, 4840245, 5128122, 5086044, 5340243 and 5274468. Every result row from the CAN serves lot=null, so no winner or value sits on any lot key, wrong or otherwise.

Separate gap, not issue 567: 72 of the 100 multi-lot CANs belong to tenders that have 2 or more lots (from the contract notice's annex B), yet their awards stay tender-scoped. Legacy R2.0.8 awards never reach a lot.

Files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-tender-db/3050fd14-5ca6-5dd7-8b63-f827e13fd8ce/scratchpad/m567/:
- part0.json: per-notice lots, awards, code_lot vs correct_lot, counts, rates
- part0_probes.jsonl: every probe
- part0_api_spotcheck.json: the 8 tender checks
- mapping.py, sampler.py, analyze_part.py: the scripts

How the sample was drawn:
- /v1/notices ignores date bounds, so the draw went through /v1/tenders?source=ted&published_after=D&published_before=D+1 instead. That lists the tenders whose current version was published on day D.
- Days: 2 random Tue–Sat days per month from 2016-01 to 2019-12, plus 4 extra days in random months (seed 567001), 100 days in total. 9 of those days returned no rows (holidays); each was replaced by the next Tue–Sat day in the same month.
- Per day: rows with lots>=2 were shuffled and tender details read in that order. The first tender whose current-version notice had at least 2 lot_results of its own was kept, provided /v1/notices/{id}/content showed at least 2 LotResult sections. One hit per day.
- Totals: 166 tender details checked, 100 multi-lot CANs read (78 R2.0.9, 22 R2.0.8), 780 award blocks. 558 GETs at 1.6 s spacing, no non-200 responses.
- /v1/notices/{id}/content is the parsed layer the projection reads, not the raw XML.

How the mapping was re-implemented:
- read_legacy_results builds lot_by_no from every Lot-kind section's TED-LOT_NO, TED-LOT_NUMBER and TED-ITEM values, first value wins.
- Each award block then sets lot_key from each of its own LOT_NO, LOT_NUMBER and ITEM values, last one wins. It is set to None when the last value is not in the map.
- The "correct" lot is the section whose LOT_NO matches the award block's LOT_NO: exact match first, then a normalized match (for '1.', '01', 'Pakiet nr 1').

Value order (this matters for the fix):
- Production does not project from the walker's output. It reads the parsed layer back from the store (Db::parsed_by_ids / parsed_chunk_on). notice_ids has PRIMARY KEY (notice_id, section_id, field_id, ordinal), and the reads come back in that index order.
- So section ids compare as text (LOT-1 < LOT-10 < LOT-2), and within a section ITEM comes before LOT_NO. Below 10 lot sections this is the same as document order; at 10 or more it is not.
- The index-order re-implementation predicts the API's lot for all 780 award blocks. Document order predicts 779; the one miss is 19411290 RES-9.

What was counted:
- "At risk" means one key string (a lot section's ITEM or LOT_NO) is claimed by two different lot sections: 5 notices. 11 notices have some section whose ITEM differs from its LOT_NO.
- 4 notices misattribute 1 award block each, all R2.0.9. Each was checked on /v1/tenders/{id}: the winner and value are served on the wrong LOT-k, the award block's own title matches the correct lot's title, and the correct lot has no result.
- 3 of the 4 are swapped or out-of-order lot numbering. The fourth (19411290) is ascending numbering with a skipped lot, which the issue calls harmless; it only goes wrong because of the text sort of section ids at 10 or more lots.
- The 22 R2.0.8 CANs carry no lot sections at all, so every result gets lot None. They cannot be hit by this bug.

Related problems found along the way (not wrong-lot cases):
- 4 notices (10 award blocks) lose their lot link: the award's LOT_NO is spelled differently from the section's ('Pakiet nr 1' vs '1', '1.' vs '1', '01' vs '1'), so the result is attached to no lot on the API.
- 2 notices (17 award blocks) have no LOT_NO in their award blocks and are attached by the block's own position number.
- Award blocks that cover several lots in one LOT_NO ('1, 2 и 3') resolve to no lot.

parts.method:
I measured 11 of 104 sampled CANs (2020-2023, all R2.0.9) with at least one award attached to the wrong lot, and the API confirms every case.

How I drew the sample: 104 OJ S days, 2 random Mon-Fri days per month for 2020-01..2023-12 plus 8 extra days (seed 567002). I used Mon-Fri because OJ S has no Saturday issue from 2019; part 1's 2019 Saturdays had no rows. A day with no TED rows was replaced by the next Mon-Fri day of the same month (5 replacements). For each day I read /v1/tenders?source=ted&published_after=D&published_before=D+1, all pages. That gives the tenders whose current version was published that day. I kept rows with lots>=2 and notice_subtype null (legacy), shuffled them with a per-day seed, and read up to 12 in turn. I kept the first one whose current notice has at least 2 of its own lot_results and whose /content is legacy (RES-n sections, TED-* fields) with at least 2 LotResult sections. Every one of the 104 days yielded one CAN: 27/25/26/26 by year, R2.0.9 S03/S04/S05 = 31/19/54, and no R2.0.8 in this period. The 104 CANs have 682 award blocks; 672 carry a LOT_NO.

Caveats on the draw: it takes one CAN per day, so it is day-weighted rather than CAN-weighted. It only covers tenders whose current version is the CAN. /content is the parsed layer, which is exactly what read_legacy_results reads; the API serves no raw XML.

How I copied the code's mapping: lot_by_no is built from Id values TED-LOT_NO, TED-LOT_NUMBER and TED-ITEM whose own section is Lot, LotsGroup or Part, and the first section to claim a key wins. Values are read in Db::parsed_by_ids order, which is the notice_ids primary-key index order (section_id, field_id, ordinal). So sections come as LOT-1, LOT-10, ..., LOT-2, and TED-ITEM comes before TED-LOT_NO. For each LotResult, every TED-LOT_NO/LOT_NUMBER/ITEM value sets lot_key = lot_by_no.get(trim). The last one wins, so the block's LOT_NO decides, and a value missing from the map resets lot_key to None.

What I counted as correct: the award block's own LOT_NO maps to the lot section with that LOT_NO, matched exactly first, then ignoring leading zeros and a 'Lot' prefix. ITEM is used only when no lot section carries a LOT_NO.

Check of the copy: my predicted lot_key matched the API's /v1/tenders/{id} lot_results[].lot for all 682 blocks. That includes 7 notices where the index order and the r209 walker's document order give different answers. Document order would have predicted wrongly there, so index order is what production actually ran.

Counts: 'at risk' means one lot section's ITEM equals another section's LOT_NO, so two sections claim the same key: 13/104. A further 7 have ITEM != LOT_NO only through zero-padding ('01' vs '1'), with no collision; that makes 20 with any ITEM != LOT_NO. Misattributed: 11/104. 2 of the 13 at-risk notices (BG and PL) came out right because the order happened to be harmless.

Wrong blocks: 41 of 672 (6.1%). 34 of them carry winners on the wrong lot key, and 7 are no-award (clos-nw) decisions on the wrong lot.

By country: 7 of the 7 Romanian (RO and LV/RO) CANs are misattributed, plus FR 3/25 and MK 1/1.

3 of the 11 (one each from FR 2020, MK 2023, FR 2023) happen only because LOT-1x sorts before LOT-2..9. In those, the lot numbering is ascending but shifted (ITEM 7-9 carrying LOT_NO 10-12). Under document order there would be 8, not 11.

API confirmation: on /v1/tenders/{tender}, lot_results[key=RES-k].lot is the wrong LOT-k and carries the block's winners and decision, and the lot_details titles show the mismatch. Award values are not served per lot (awarded is null and result_value has lot null), so I could show a value only from the block in /content, not on a lot on the API. I dropped /v1/lots?tender=&winner= as a check: on /v1/lots, winner filters by the lot's Tender and returns every lot.

verdict.why:
The claim is confirmed. I checked it against the live API and against the code.

What the notice says (GET /v1/notices/19411290/content; 305919-2017, R2.0.9.S02.E01):
- There are 13 lot sections. LOT-1 to LOT-5 have ITEM equal to LOT_NO.
- From LOT-6 on, LOT_NO is ITEM+1. LOT-9 is ITEM 9, LOT_NO 10, 'Revêtements de sols souples'. LOT-10 is ITEM 10, LOT_NO 11, 'Plomberie — sanitaire — chauffage central gaz — vmc'.
- Award block RES-9 has ITEM 9, LOT_NO 10, title 'Revêtements de sols souples', contractor ORG-10 'Renard Jacques' and VAL_TOTAL EUR 1187546 cents (11,875.46).
- RES-10 has LOT_NO 11 and was won by Boschung for 89,140.00.

What the API serves (GET /v1/tenders/5984445):
- lot_results lists {key:RES-9, lot:LOT-10, awarded 1187546 EUR, winners [Renard Jacques]}, and RES-10 is also on LOT-10.
- parties lists two LOT-10 winners, Renard Jacques and Boschung, and no party or result on LOT-9.
- lot_details and /v1/lots?tender=5984445 confirm LOT-9 is 'Revêtements de sols souples' and LOT-10 is 'Plomberie…'.
- So RES-9's winner and value sit on a lot whose published LOT_NO is 11, while the award block's LOT_NO is 10.

Why the code does this (crates/ingest/src/project.rs read_legacy_results, around lines 7114-7151):
- `lot_by_no` puts each lot section's TED-LOT_NO, TED-LOT_NUMBER and TED-ITEM values into one map with `or_insert`, so the first section to claim a key keeps it.
- Each award block then sets `lot_key` from its own ITEM and LOT_NO values in turn, so whichever comes last wins.
- TED-ITEM is the walker's ITEM attribute (crates/ingest/src/r209/parse.rs, around line 344), which every section carries.

The order the projection reads values in:
- The projection's batch reader is Db::parsed_by_ids in crates/store/src/canonical.rs (around line 14770). It runs `SELECT ... FROM notice_ids WHERE notice_id IN (...)` with no ORDER BY.
- notice_ids has PRIMARY KEY (notice_id, section_id, field_id, ordinal), so if the planner walks that index, rows come back with section_id sorted as text (LOT-10 to LOT-13 before LOT-2 to LOT-9) and TED-ITEM before TED-LOT_NO inside each section.
- I am inferring that the planner uses that index. Nothing pins the order, but it is the only order I found that explains what the API serves.

Tracing the map in that order:
- LOT-10's ITEM claims '10', then its LOT_NO claims '11'.
- LOT-6 claims '6' and '7', LOT-7 claims '8', and LOT-8 claims '9'.
- When LOT-9 comes up, its ITEM '9' and LOT_NO '10' are both taken already.
- RES-9's last id value is LOT_NO '10', which maps to LOT-10, so it lands on the wrong lot.
- Every other block resolves correctly. That is exactly the pattern the API shows: LOT-10 carries RES-9 and RES-10, and LOT-9 has nothing.

In document order (LOT-1 to LOT-13, ITEM emitted at section open, before LOT_NO) the same map would resolve RES-9 correctly to LOT-9. The read order is what triggers this case, and the shared ITEM/LOT_NO map is the bug underneath it.

The parsed-content summary is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-tender-db/3050fd14-5ca6-5dd7-8b63-f827e13fd8ce/scratchpad/m567/dl/content.xml. Despite the .xml name it is the /content JSON, not the published XML. The tender and lots responses are tender.json and lots.json in the same dl folder.

verdict.why:
I checked this against the live API (one GET at a time, at least 2 s apart) and against the code, and the claim holds.

1) The published structure. Note that /v1/notices/20128178/content returns the parsed sections as JSON, not the raw XML. The notice is 501322-2018, profile ted-export-r209, version R2.0.9.S03.E01, with five lot sections:
- LOT-1: ITEM 1, LOT_NO 4, 'Arhiva de reviste Wiley Journal Backfiles'
- LOT-2: ITEM 2, LOT_NO 2
- LOT-3: ITEM 3, LOT_NO 3
- LOT-4: ITEM 4, LOT_NO 1, 'Arhiva de reviste Science Direct Backfiles'
- LOT-5: ITEM 5, LOT_NO 5

Award block RES-2 has ITEM 2, LOT_NO 1, the title 'Arhiva de reviste Science Direct Backfiles', the contractor ORG-3 and VAL_TOTAL 1450200000 cents (RON 14,502,000). RES-5 has ITEM 5, LOT_NO 4, the title 'Wiley Journal Backfiles' and 860000000 cents.

2) What the API serves. /v1/tenders/6352468 lot_results puts RES-2 on lot "LOT-1": awarded 1450200000 RON, winner E-Nformation (org 12516025). RES-5 is also on "LOT-1". No lot_result points at LOT-4. The parties list shows two E-Nformation winner rows on LOT-1 and none on LOT-4. /v1/lots?tender=6352468 confirms LOT-1 is 'Wiley Journal Backfiles' (published LOT_NO 4) and LOT-4 is 'Science Direct Backfiles' (published LOT_NO 1). So the award's winner and value appear on a lot whose published LOT_NO (4) differs from the block's own LOT_NO (1).

3) The mechanism in /home/user/tender-db/crates/ingest/src/project.rs read_legacy_results (lines 7114-7151).
- The walker in /home/user/tender-db/crates/ingest/src/r209/parse.rs (lines 344-349) emits TED-ITEM on the section when it opens it, before the children's TED-LOT_NO, and pushes values in document order.
